evidence_items.summary: ABSTRACT Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) burdens the healthcare system, affecting millions of individuals worldwide with a potential progression to complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The World Health Organization launched the chronic viral hepatitis elimination plan which aimed to eliminate chronic hepatitis B virus by 2030, yet the goal has seemed to be far from reach with the remaining few years owing to different hurdles ranging from screening strategy and diagnosis to risk stratification for antiviral treatment and HCC surveillance. To refine the management of CHB, previous studies focused on identifying the at‐risk populations and predictors for adverse outcomes using conventional statistical methods. With the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI), there is further room to improve different aspects of screening and management. For instance, generative AI, such as large language models (LLMs), has been proven to have the ability to answer different clinical questions, assisting patients' and physicians' decision on various clinical scenarios. Different machine learning and deep learning models have also been developed to assess for liver fibrosis, as well as to aid segmentation of liver structures and detection of focal liver lesions through various imaging modalities. While different AI models have shown superior performance compared to those developed through traditional statistical models, the lack of standardized datasets in training cohorts and the unresolved concerns of hallucination of false information in LLMs pose challenges on applying AI in the current management of CHB, in which further studies are required to adopt AI into daily clinical practice.
evidence_items.title: Clinical Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Chronic Hepatitis B

evidence_items.summary: UNSTRUCTURED Autism encompasses heterogeneous genetic, neurobiological, developmental, and medical pathways. Artificial intelligence (AI) has advanced autism research through multimodal analysis of eye tracking, EEG, neuroimaging, and molecular data; beyond autism, AI is also accelerating therapeutic target identification and drug discovery. Yet translating these advances into individualized, biologically informed clinical decisions remains a major challenge. We propose biologically anchored AI as a decision-oriented framework linking genetic etiology, molecular and microbiome-associated pathways, neurophysiology, digital observations, and developmental context to explicit clinical questions. We distinguish etiological characterization, exploratory mechanistic stratification, and treatment-specific response prediction; these are not interchangeable forms of validation. Examples include individualized genetic therapies, SYNGAP1-directed drug development, heterogeneous responses in fragile X and oxytocin trials, stool metabolomics, sleep EEG, and prenatal MRI. Rather than requiring comprehensive testing for every person, the approach asks whether a selected measurement improves a defined decision beyond standard assessment. Candidate subgroups and biomarkers must be replicated, tested prospectively for incremental value and, where treatment selection is proposed, evaluated for differential benefit from a specified intervention. The goal is not a new universal autism subtype or an automated treatment recommendation, but clinically meaningful, equitable, and developmentally responsive precision care.
evidence_items.title: From Autism Classification to Precision Intervention: A Biologically Anchored Artificial Intelligence Framework (Preprint)

evidence_items.summary: Accurate prediction of the in-cylinder pressure trace does not necessarily preserve pressure-derived combustion descriptors. This study uses a synthetic spark-ignition benchmark to examine whether explicit supervision of these descriptors changes surrogate accuracy. Six neural-network variants share a 5382-parameter architecture and training budget, with cumulative supervision of pressure derivatives, apparent heat release, peak descriptors, combustion phasing and gross indicated work. The benchmark comprises 960 operating points divided into training, validation, interpolation and simultaneous speed–load extrapolation sets, plus a closure-shift test with altered combustion and wall-heat-transfer relations. At the specified 1° output resolution, validation-selected A4 reduces interpolation CA50 mean absolute error from 0.0938° to 0.0688° and maximum pressure-rise-rate (MPRR) error from 0.0506 to 0.0303 bar/°, corresponding to improvements of 26.6% and 40.1%. Pressure RMSE increases from 0.0980 to 0.1031 bar, and gross IMEP error increases from 0.0296 to 0.0529 bar. A4 retains a lower MPRR error during speed–load extrapolation, with higher pressure and work errors, while all models deteriorate under the closure shift. The 1° MPRR discretisation discrepancy of 0.01702 bar/° is comparable in magnitude to the 0.0203 bar/° model improvement. These results establish a redistribution of approximation error within the prescribed benchmark. The fixed geometry, nominal fuel and simplified single-zone generator, together with the absence of experimental validation, preclude interpreting the reported gains as demonstrated improvements on real engines.
evidence_items.title: Derivative and Combustion Metric Supervised Cylinder Pressure Surrogates for Spark-Ignition Engines: A Synthetic Benchmark Study

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Automated regression testing is essential for maintaining rapid, high-quality delivery in Agile and Scrum organizations. Many teams, including Hacon (a Siemens company), face a persistent gap: validated test specifications accumulate faster than they are automated, limiting regression coverage and increasing manual work. This paper reports an exploratory industrial case study of the Hacon Test Automation Copilot, an agentic AI system that generates system-level regression test scripts from validated specifications using retrieval-augmented generation and a multi-agent workflow. Integrated with Hacon’s CI pipelines, the Copilot operates asynchronously as a “silent AI teammate”, producing candidate scripts for human review. Mixed-method evaluation shows the AI accelerates script authoring and increases throughput, with 30–50% code reuse. However, human review remains necessary for maintainability and correct domain interpretation. Clear specifications, explicit governance, and ongoing human–AI collaboration are critical. We conclude with lessons for scaling regression automation and enabling effective human–AI teaming in Agile settings.
evidence_items.title: Human–AI Collaboration for Scaling Agile Regression Testing: An Agentic-AI Teammate from Manual to Automated Testing

evidence_items.summary: Objective: To determine the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) for assessing myometrial invasion, cervical invasion, and lymph node metastasis in endometrial carcinoma and to evaluate their association with postoperative histopathological findings. Methodology: This Prospective Longitudinal Study was conducted in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Ayub Teaching Hospital, Abbottabad, Pakistan, from January to December 2025. Following institutional Ethical Review Committee approval, 144 patients with biopsy-proven endometrial carcinoma underwent pelvic CE-MRI within one month before surgery. We assessed myometrial invasion, cervical invasion, and lymph node metastasis on T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images. We used histopathological findings as the definitive reference standard. We used correlation analysis to assess associations between MRI and histopathological findings, and logistic regression to evaluate factors associated with positive pelvic lymph nodes. Results: For detecting myometrial invasion, cervical invasion, and lymph node metastasis, CE-MRI showed sensitivities of 85.71%, 90.9%, and 85.7% and specificities of 89.47%, 100%, and 79.6%, respectively. Histopathological lymph node metastasis was strongly associated with ≥50% myometrial invasion (100% sensitivity, 97.9% specificity), whereas the association with cervical invasion was poor. In univariate analysis, disease stage, tumor grade and type, positive peritoneal cytology, myometrial invasion, and cervical stromal invasion were significantly associated with lymph node involvement. Conclusion: CE-MRI demonstrated good diagnostic performance for assessing local tumor invasion and lymph node metastasis. Patients with <50% myometrial invasion and no cervical invasion on CE-MRI may have a lower likelihood of lymph node metastasis, potentially supporting individualized surgical planning
evidence_items.title: Contrast-Enhanced MRI in The Preoperative Evaluation of Endometrial Carcinoma

evidence_items.summary: Large audio language models (LALMs) have shown impressive capabilities on diverse audio understanding tasks, ranging from speech transcription to music analysis. However, because LALMs are typically trained to produce text-aligned responses, their hidden states are progressively shaped for text generation rather than for preserving acoustic information. As a result, the diverse acoustic content that audio carries, such as phonetic detail, prosody, sound events, affect, and pitch, is lost along the way and difficult to leverage in the response. We introduce Continuous Audio Thinking (CoAT), a framework that equips audio language models with a continuous latent workspace for organizing acoustic information prior to response generation, grounded by distillation from audio experts. Within the thinking space, the model can utilize the rich acoustic information provided by expert distillation when generating its response. Furthermore, the proposed continuous thinking block can be processed in a single prefill, so CoAT does not require additional autoregressive decoding cost over the baseline. Across three LALMs, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, and Audio Flamingo~3, performance gains on a broad benchmark suite spanning audio reasoning, audio understanding, music classification, speech emotion, and speech transcription demonstrate the effectiveness of CoAT. Further analysis confirms that the auxiliary supervision propagates from the thinking positions to the model's textual responses.
evidence_items.title: Continuous Audio Thinking for Large Audio Language Models

evidence_items.summary: The extraction of critical information from crime-related documents is a crucial task for law enforcement agencies. The extraction of this information can be interpreted as a Named-Entity Recognition (NER) task. However, there is a considerable lack of adequately annotated data on general real-world crime scenarios. To address this issue, we present CrimeNER, a case study of crime-related NER, and a general crime-related Named-Entity Recognition database (CrimeNER-db), consisting of more than 1.5K annotated documents extracted from public reports of terrorist attacks and the US Department of Justice's press notes. We define 4 coarse types of crime entity and 21 fine-grained entity types. We address the quality of the presented database with fully supervised experiments using flat and nested NER architectures and zero- and few-shot experiments using Large Language Models (LLMs). The database is available on GitHub.
evidence_items.title: CrimeNER: Curated Dataset and Methods for Research and Investigation in Language Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Codes of professional ethics guide and restrict specialists, who increasingly work with assistants built on large language models. Such an assistant can breach the user's code, or help the user breach it, without the user noticing. Evaluations reporting broad categories of harm cannot show how often this happens or which provision is breached. TenetBench pairs 3,433 requests conflicting with clauses of fifteen Russian-language professional codes with benign twins that differ only in the legitimacy of what is asked. An automated pipeline generates the tasks from the text of a code, so the corpus grows with every code added and a provision yields new tasks on every run. It also produced tasks and human-validated verdicts from two English codes of other jurisdictions. In human validation of the frozen pipeline, specialists rated 0.995 of the conflicting tasks plausible, and the model judge agreed with the adjudicated label at Gwet's AC1 of at least 0.894 on 1,860 elements. We evaluated fourteen model and reasoning-mode combinations on whether they produce the conflicting text, decline or warn. Eleven of the fourteen produce conflicting content on most such requests, mostly without a warning, and nearly three warnings in four accompany conflicting content. The models that conform more do so by declining while still serving the legitimate twin, and enabling reasoning halved the refusals of two models. We hope the dataset and pipeline will help evaluate how language models observe professional norms and let diagnostic datasets be built for particular professions and organisations.
evidence_items.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics

evidence_items.summary: Agentic AI systems pursue goals through multi-step planning, tool use, memory, and adaptive action, creating governance challenges that differ from those associated with conventional predictive or generative AI. This study systematically reviews governance evidence relevant to agentic AI in Africa and develops an Ubuntu-informed conceptual framework. Following PRISMA 2020, 91 records published from 2019 to April 2026 were analysed through quantitative content analysis and abductive thematic synthesis. The corpus comprises 12 agentic-AI-specific records, 3 agentic-adjacent records, and 76 broader AI-governance records used as contextual evidence. Five literature-derived gaps were identified: accountability across autonomous action chains, infrastructure-aware oversight, bias and representational harm, policy fragmentation, and community exclusion. These findings inform five proposed governance elements: communal impact assessment, collective consent and participation, infrastructure-contingent oversight, African dataset and bias auditing, and communal accountability. The framework is a literature-derived conceptual proposition, not an empirically validated governance instrument, and requires future case-study, expert-panel, and comparative policy testing.
evidence_items.title: Governing Agentic AI in Africa: A Systematic Literature Review of Ethical Challenges, Framework Gaps, and Ubuntu-Informed Governance Solutions

evidence_items.summary: Open multimodal reasoning models have benefited from large-scale reasoning supervision, yet reliable post-training remains challenging due to uneven data quality, inefficient supervision construction, imbalanced difficulty, and cross-domain interference. We introduce MMVistaReason (MVR), an open-data post-training recipe with three components: (1) broader capability coverage across complementary Analytical and Real-World reasoning groups, emphasizing structured reasoning versus visual perception and spatial grounding; (2) efficient SFT and RL data construction, standardizing heterogeneous open data through staged cleaning and annotation, combining difficulty-aware cascaded teacher distillation with answer-likelihood-based trajectory selection to construct MVR-SFT-528K, and applying scale-specific frontier filtering for MVR-RL-63K; and (3) specialize-then-integrate training, which trains complementary RL experts and consolidates their capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Our analyses reveal a capacity-dependent interaction between supervision difficulty, trajectory quality, and model capacity: smaller students benefit more from selected supervision, while larger students are robust to trajectory variation and mixed-domain interference. Mixed-domain RL introduces benchmark-level negative transfer, whereas MOPD provides consistent capability integration, with the preferred KL direction varying across model scales. Across 15 multimodal benchmarks, MVR-4B achieves an average score of 72.8, outperforming Qwen3.5-9B (Instruct) and MMFineReason-8B while using about 70% fewer samples than MMFineReason. Scaling to 9B improves the average to 74.4, surpassing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (Instruct). Overall, MMVistaReason demonstrates that systematic open-data construction and capacity-aware post-training provide a practical and scalable path toward reliable multimodal reasoning.
evidence_items.title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning

evidence_items.summary: The growth of time-series datasets and foundation models has made dataset comparison a central part of time-series workflows. Assessing source-target transfer before model adaptation requires similarity estimates that can summarize transfer-related dataset relationships without exhaustive source-target evaluation over every candidate pair. Many metrics have been proposed for measuring similarity between time-series datasets, but they capture different dataset relationships and vary in how well they align with downstream utility across tasks. We evaluate this gap by measuring the correlation between source-target similarity scores and downstream forecasting errors in out-of-distribution and transfer-learning settings. We propose Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost (DISC), a learnable aggregation framework that uses calibration transfer observations to select, weight, and combine similarity metrics for different downstream tasks. By integrating complementary metric values, DISC better distinguishes source-target dataset differences that matter for downstream behavior. After calibration, DISC scores source-target pairs using only their similarity-metric values and yields higher alignment than single-metric references on the reported split. These results show that time-series dataset similarity is task-dependent, and that learned metric integration provides a stronger proxy for downstream transfer behavior than manually selecting one similarity metric.
evidence_items.title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset

evidence_items.summary: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.
evidence_items.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models

evidence_items.summary: Fine-grained multimodal intelligence requires models to both understand a designated region and localize it from language. Existing methods learn these directions with separate objectives and task-specific annotations. We present Generalized CycleGRPO, the first unified reinforcement learning framework coupling region understanding and localization across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal domains. Given a region, a multimodal large language model generates candidate descriptions and then localizes each description to reconstruct the input region. Reconstruction overlap provides a verifiable reward for captioning, while individual localization rewards improve the inverse mapping. A common region-space formulation extends this cycle from image masks and boxes to video intervals and timestamped spatial evidence, without reference captions or an external language-model judge during reinforcement learning. In videos, the cycle encourages descriptions that distinguish a target event from similar recurrences. We introduce DOVE (Distinctive Occurrence-level Video-caption Evaluation), a human-verified contrastive benchmark for this temporal distinctiveness. CycleGRPO improves SAMTok's overall gIoU from 57.5% to 68.2% on GroundingSuite and average gIoU from 71.2% to 78.7% on GRES. For temporal tasks, it achieves 51.9% tIoU on Charades and 33.3% Temporal Evidence Coverage on DOVE, compared with 45.6% and 14.8% for the Qwen3-VL initialization. These results establish region-text cycle consistency as a general self-evaluation principle for multimodal understanding and localization. Models, code, and DOVE are available at https://devinxzhang.github.io/Generalized-CycleGRPO-Page/.
evidence_items.title: Generalized CycleGRPO for Fine-Grained Multimodal Understanding and Grounding

evidence_items.summary: Language models can make personalized recommendations from rich item content, user history, and feedback. However, evaluating many candidates with full-text inputs incurs substantial online computation and limits serving throughput. We introduce DuoLM, a framework for fast and effective personalized recommendation that integrates a compact recommendation model with an efficient serving runtime. An encoder LLM learns compact item representations for offline reuse, while a personalized ranker LLM combines them with user history and feedback for recommendation. We train both models end to end with recommendation supervision and teacher distillation. The runtime further accelerates inference through virtual token IDs for embedding access, shared history computation, and CUDA Graph replay. Benchmark results show that our framework achieves recommendation quality comparable to that of the expert teacher model. On a single H100, it delivers approximately 26,400 candidate scores per second, about 60times the throughput of the teacher served with vLLM and automatic prefix caching.
evidence_items.title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Music source separation (MSS) has been conventionally addressed by discriminative methods. Recently, flow matching has emerged as a strong generative paradigm for modeling complex data distributions, with successful applications across diverse domains. These advances motivate us to systematically investigate flow matching for MSS in a four-source (Vocals, Bass, Drums, Other) setting in full-band stereo. Specifically, we investigate prediction targets, flow paths, single-source versus multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency constraints. Beyond the signal-level metrics commonly used for MSS, such as signal-to-distortion ratio, we further evaluate MSS methods using embedding-based metrics, as well as a listening test, providing a comprehensive benchmark. On MUSDB18-HQ, our proposed model exhibits competitive performance in both objective and subjective tests, highlighting the potential of flow matching for generative MSS. Demo: https://ik4sumii.github.io/FLOMSS/
evidence_items.title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching

evidence_items.summary: This narrative review examines large language model (LLM) assistance with archaeological literature, code, metadata, and transcription, together with the ethical, legal, and governance conditions on its use. I propose a Zotero Model Context Protocol (MCP) citation-review sequence that records the publication version, source evidence, provisional assessment, and review status. A small case study tests source reading with sixty constructed claims about ten randomly selected papers cited in this manuscript. Ten model-and-reasoning configurations assessed the claims against my human reference judgments. Exact label agreement ranged from 80.0% to 100.0%, with nine configurations matching at least 58 of sixty labels. One evaluator reported the correct source values but selected the wrong label; a matching label could also accompany an inadequate page locator. The study used a controlled PDF interface, one human reviewer, and one run per configuration, and did not test the full Zotero workflow. I recommend establishing permission to process research materials and checking outputs against inspectable evidence. LLM-supplied citations require human source review; citations selected through the author’s own reading can receive an LLM audit, with human follow-up on disagreements, unresolved support, and proposed changes.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Models in Archaeological Practice: Efficacy, Ethics, Risks, and Governance

evidence_items.summary: In this paper, a semi-deterministic approach is introduced for evaluating the answer-and-reasoning reliability of large language models using propositional logic and Bernoulli random variables. We focus on an operational class of hallucination defined by failures in final-answer correctness and/or reasoning validity, which is distinct from factuality hallucination involving fabricated world knowledge. Hallucination is represented as the logical negation of the conjunction of answer correctness and reasoning validity, enabling probabilistic evaluation. The framework was evaluated using Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 5 on probability and random process (PRP) problems. For each model, 90 questions were presented in five cycles per condition, producing 450 responses per model-condition combination and 1800 responses in total. The Independent and Persistent conditions differed in conversational state, session structure, and question-order structure; therefore, observed differences are interpreted as condition-level associations. For Gemini 3.1 Pro, the hallucination probability increased from 20.44% to 36.22% (77.2% relative increase), while for Claude Sonnet 5, it increased from 22.44% to 36.22% (61.4% relative increase). A dependence-aware generalized estimating equation analysis estimated an odds ratio of 2.080 (95% robust CI [1.384, 3.127], p=4.264×10−4) for Persistent versus Independent conditions.
evidence_items.title: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models: A Probabilistic Study of Context Persistence Effects

evidence_items.summary: The public release of ChatGPT on 30 November 2022, constituted an inflection point in the history of artificial intelligence applied to medicine. Within oncology, a specialty defined by the need to synthesize complex, heterogeneous, and rapidly evolving clinical data, large language models [LLMs] have transitioned within a remarkably compressed timeline from objects of academic curiosity to the threshold of institutional deployment. This narrative review maps the trajectory of LLM integration across the oncological care continuum, from patient-facing information tools to multidisciplinary tumor board decision support. The clinical landscape is organized around a three-tier framework of readiness: domains in which LLMs demonstrate consistent supportive performance across predominantly retrospective, benchmark-based, and early implementation studies; domains in which early evidence is promising but prospective validation is lacking; and domains that remain aspirational and require substantial technical and regulatory development before adoption can be responsibly recommended. A dedicated analysis is presented of the mechanistic distinction between static parametric knowledge and dynamic retrieval-augmented generation [RAG], the probabilistic origins of factual inaccuracy in language model outputs, and the role of authoritative guideline grounding in constructing trustworthy AI architectures for oncology. The review examines how multimodal LLMs [MLLMs] are beginning to integrate radiomics, whole-slide pathology imaging [WSI], next-generation sequencing [NGS] data, transcriptomics, and proteomics into unified oncological reasoning workflows and how this convergence informs the precision oncology vision.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Models in Oncology: Current Applications, Evidence Gaps, and Implementation Requirements—A Narrative Review

evidence_items.summary: Chinese dialect recognition by large language models (LLMs) cannot be evaluated adequately by terminal-label accuracy alone because correct labels may still rely on weak evidence, faulty knowledge mapping, or poorly calibrated uncertainty. We present DIKWP-3No-4S as a semantic white-box evaluation framework in which externally coded semantic relations and scoring rules are inspectable, while the evaluated LLM remains a black box. The original controlled experiment used six foundational cases across Clean and three 3-No conditions, generating 270 repeated observations. To strengthen prospective assessment of the framework, we added 18 new independent cases with reference standards frozen before response collection. Three LLMs were tested under Clean and one preassigned 3-No perturbation, yielding 108 responses independently blind-rated by two experts. Case-level permutation tests, case-clustered bootstrap intervals, and Holm correction showed stable terminal-label accuracy but significant changes in judgment-boundary and condition-adaptation scores. Inter-rater analysis showed strong consistency for judgment-boundary and condition-adaptation scores, whereas several fine-grained semantic measures, including evidence-explanation quality, D → D activation, path quality, and SemA, showed low or near-zero inter-rater reliability and are therefore treated as exploratory rather than validated measures. These results support DIKWP-3No-4S for external semantic auditing and fault localization, but do not establish an independent terminal-performance advantage from DIKWP structuring.
evidence_items.title: A DIKWP-3No-4S Semantic White-Box Evaluation Framework for Chinese Dialect Recognition by Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been applied as a novel and accessible alternative to traditional machine learning (ML). Their main advantage lies in the fact that they do not require model training or data pre-processing; instead, they are guided through natural language instructions. In this study, we evaluate the suitability of LLMs for corrosion-related tasks and introduce an approach that combines LLMs with hard-coded logic to enhance reliability and performance. The methodology was tested on three tasks: classifying images of organic coatings in ‘blister’/‘no blister’ classes, ranking specimens based on corrosion severity, and classifying images into severity classes. The results demonstrate performance comparable to that of trained ML models, with ‘blister’/‘no blister’ classification achieving accuracies up to 0.93. These findings highlight the potential of LLMs, when integrated with expert-driven strategies, as practical and scalable tools for corrosion assessment.
evidence_items.title: Exploring the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for corrosion-related tasks: Using large language models (LLMs) to analyse organic coatings images

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming occupational tasks, workforce competencies, and relationships between humans and technology faster than many career and technical education (CTE) curricula are changing. This theoretical article introduces the Adaptive CTE Renewal Framework to address the growing mismatch between legacy curriculum and AI-transformed work. Drawing on human capital theory, sociotechnical systems theory, institutional theory and path dependence, and adult/workforce learning theory, the framework conceptualizes curriculum renewal across five interacting dimensions: occupational transformation, curriculum currency, faculty capability alignment, program architecture, and external alignment. Six leadership tests are proposed for evaluating whether courses should be retained, revised, integrated, replaced, or retired. The article argues that conventional periodic curriculum review is increasingly inadequate under conditions of continuous technological disruption and proposes continuous curriculum intelligence as an alternative institutional paradigm. Ultimately, CTE relevance depends on institutions' capacity to continuously align curriculum, faculty expertise, program structures, stakeholder evidence, and workforce competencies with evolving occupational realities.
evidence_items.title: When Legacy Curriculum Meets Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence workloads and cloud services require increasingly sophisticated resource allocation, yet conventional scheduling policies may optimize utilization or response time without explicitly accounting for energy consumption and carbon intensity. This paper proposes a Green Artificial Intelligence framework for intelligent resource management that combines workload prediction, energy-aware optimization, service-level constraints, and runtime feedback. The framework estimates near-term demand from system telemetry and selects resource allocations that balance performance, energy use, and operational cost. A carbon-aware objective can incorporate time-varying grid carbon intensity where trustworthy data are available. The proposed evaluation uses trace-driven experiments and a reproducible comparison against static allocation, utilization-based autoscaling, and energy-unaware scheduling. Key measures include energy per completed task, average and tail latency, SLA violation rate, resource utilization, and estimated carbon emissions. A public cloud workload trace and a documented power-measurement model are recommended for implementation in Python. Because no implementation, trace processing, or experiments have been executed for this manuscript, all quantitative results are left pending.
evidence_items.title: GREEN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR INTELLIGENT RESOURCE MANAGEMENT

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by the public and healthcare professionals for clinical reasoning. However, they were developed as general-purpose language models rather than dedicated clinical decision-support tools, and their performance in real-world acute heart failure (AHF) management remains insufficiently evaluated. We compared four contemporary AI models with physician decision-making. Methods This single-center retrospective observational study incorporated a cross-sectional AI evaluation of consecutive patients treated at Sotiria General Hospital between July and November 2025, excluding acute coronary syndrome. ChatGPT, ChatGPT Plus, DeepSeek, and an ESC guideline-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) model independently assessed identical standardized cases. Recommendations were compared with physician decisions on diagnosis, treatment, guideline-directed medical therapy, timing, and prognosis using Cohen’s kappa, McNemar’s test, Cochran’s Q, Wilcoxon signed-rank testing, and multivariable logistic regression. Results Diagnostic performance differed significantly across systems (Cochran’s Q=8.477, P=0.037). In the balanced diagnostic cohort, ChatGPT Plus achieved the highest HF accuracy (accuracy 86.5%; sensitivity 87.0%, specificity 86.0%), followed by RAG (accuracy 77.5%), ChatGPT (accuracy 77.0%), and DeepSeek (accuracy 69.0%). For HF within the top three differential diagnoses, sensitivity was 90.0–97.0%; specificity was 70.0% for ChatGPT Plus, 68.0% for RAG, 19.0% for DeepSeek, and 15.0% for ChatGPT. Physician agreement was highest for guideline-directed therapies, with greater variability in prognosis and escalation of care. RAG more closely matched physician therapeutic timing but did not consistently outperform general-purpose models.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Physician Decision-Making in Acute Heart Failure: A Comparative Evaluation of Four Contemporary AI Systems

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Patients increasingly form expectations about plastic surgery from social media and other online sources, and artificial intelligence (AI) now functions both as a tool for analyzing that content and as a source of the content itself. This review maps original empirical studies that applied an AI or computational method beyond conventional statistical analysis to social media, online reviews, public digital images, surveys, or crowdsourced data in plastic surgery while reporting an outcome related to the perceptions, questions, experiences, or information exposure of patients or the public. Twenty-six studies published between 2019 and 2026 met inclusion criteria, 19 (73%) of them since 2024. Facial aesthetic surgery was the most represented domain (n = 9; 35%). RealSelf was the most common primary data source (n = 8; 31%), 18 studies (69%) analyzed a single platform, and 18 (69%) analyzed text alone. Sentiment or emotion analysis was the most common computational method (n = 13; 50%), and 16 studies (62%) applied pretrained models or lexicons as released, without training on study data. A human comparator was reported in 10 studies (38%) and external validation in 1 (4%). No study linked patient-generated digital data to a validated patient-reported outcome measure or evaluated these data for surgical education. Work at this intersection is expanding rapidly but remains descriptive, single-platform, and largely unvalidated.
evidence_items.title: Emerging Artificial Intelligence: A New Digital Age Across The Aesthetic Landscape

evidence_items.summary: Industry 4.0 integrates cyber–physical systems, industrial Internet of Things technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and real-time analytics to improve manufacturing performance. However, small- and medium-scale manufacturing facilities frequently face fragmented automation, reactive maintenance, and limited integration between production data and operational decision-making. This study developed and experimentally evaluated an AI-enabled Digital Twin (DT) framework for optimizing a multi-station mechanical manufacturing system in Bangladesh. The manufacturing cell comprised six interconnected stations: raw-material inspection and sorting, automated loading and orientation, CNC machining, drilling and cutting, AI-assisted quality inspection, and automated storage and dispatch. A synchronized DT represented machine states, production flow, queue formation, operating parameters, energy consumption, tool condition, vibration, temperature, and quality outcomes. An AI layer supported anomaly detection and cycle-time prediction, while a multi-objective optimization mechanism balanced throughput and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) against cycle time, energy consumption, defect rate, and unplanned downtime. Three operating configurations were evaluated: conventional programmable logic controller (PLC)-based operation, DT-assisted operation, and DT–AI optimization. During the six-hour production period, the DT–AI configuration increased throughput from 338 to 405 parts, reduced average cycle time from 63.9 to 53.3 s/part, and increased OEE from 67.6% to 84.6%. Energy consumption decreased from 54.8 to 47.6 kWh, the defect rate declined from 5.9% to 2.6%, and unplanned downtime decreased from 38.4 to 17.9 min. The anomaly classifier achieved an accuracy of 94.6%, while the cycle-time prediction model achieved a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.94.
evidence_items.title: Digital Twin-Driven Optimization of Mechanical Manufacturing Systems Using Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI), especially generative AI, is transforming how higher-education institutions design instruction, support learners, evaluate knowledge, and structure academic work. In this paper, we review the implications of AI for teaching in universities, drawing upon contemporary scholarship, international guidance and select technical studies of service-oriented architectures, process modeling, database design and graph-based analytics. We performed a structured narrative review guided by a priori concepts of AI-supported personalization, tutoring, assessment, educator workload, academic integrity, privacy, bias and institutional governance. Evidence suggests that artificial intelligence can help improve access to timely feedback, adaptive support, course design and reduce routine workload. But access to a general-purpose model does not necessarily produce learning: benefits depend on pedagogical scaffolding, course alignment, verification, and ongoing supervision by humans. The key risks are: generated or biased outputs, cognitive offloading, unequal access, opaque data practices, and unreliable authorship judgments. The paper concludes that AI should be deployed as an augmentative educational infrastructure, not as a replacement for teachers. To ensure that technological efficiency benefits real learning and academic principles, universities need to combine AI literacy, redesigned assessment, privacy-by-design, transparent policies, interoperable systems, and ongoing assessment.
evidence_items.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE TEACHING PROCESS IN HIGHER EDUCATION

organizations: University of Basra, Basra, Iraq.
evidence_items.summary: Purpose: This study aims to integrate machine learning and deep learning techniques with Digital Twin technology to improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction and support personalised clinical decision-making. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study reviews existing Digital Twin frameworks in healthcare and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven Digital Twin paradigm based on temporal electronic health record data. The proposed approach develops dynamic digital representations of patients that reflect their current health conditions and predict their future clinical evolution. Machine learning and deep learning techniques analyse large-scale medical data, identify hidden patterns, and provide early predictions of patient deterioration, particularly in intensive care environments. Research Limitation: Further validation using diverse, multi-centre clinical datasets and real-time patient information is required before the model can be widely implemented in clinical practice. Findings: The findings indicate that AI-powered Digital Twins can improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction, facilitate early identification of patient deterioration, and support clinical treatment decisions. The proposed approach may also enable proactive, personalised, and data-driven disease management. Practical Implication: The proposed Digital Twin paradigm can help healthcare professionals monitor patients, identify high-risk cases, select appropriate interventions, and allocate critical care resources more effectively. Social Implication: Improved early prediction and personalised treatment may reduce mortality rates, prevent avoidable complications, enhance healthcare quality, and reduce the clinical and economic burden on patients and healthcare institutions.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Digital Twin for Disease Progression Prediction: A Comprehensive Review

evidence_items.summary: Patch size is an important design parameter in patch-based Earth observation (EO) learning, yet it is rarely treated as an experimental variable because existing benchmarks use a single fixed scale. We introduce SENSERO, a multi-scale, multi-label Sentinel-2 benchmark for Romania consisting of 10,000 geographically fixed locations extracted at eight patch sizes, from 64×64 to 336×336 pixels, at a constant 10 m ground sampling distance, so that all scales share identical patch centres and an identical, spatially disjoint 70/15/15 partition. Each patch provides twelve-band bottom-of-atmosphere reflectance, a rasterised CORINE Land Cover (CLC) 2018 reference map from which five deterministic multi-label annotation layers are derived (three levels of the CLC hierarchy, the BigEarthNet nomenclature, and a scheme adapted to the Romanian landscape). The benchmark task is patch-level multi-label classification; the rasterised reference maps serve to derive and trace the labels, not as a segmentation target. Using ResNet-50 baselines trained from scratch, we find that larger patches bring little benefit at CLC Level 1 but clear gains at Levels 2 and 3 (macro mAP at Level 3 rising from 0.42 at 64 px to 0.61 at 336 px), with per-location gains saturating around 224–256 pixels; that transfer across scales is asymmetric, models trained on wide patches transferring to narrow ones far better than the reverse; and that the choice of nomenclature affects measured performance as much as patch size. Leave-scene-out cross-validation, an ablation of the labelling rule, pretrained ResNet-50 and ViT-S/16 controls and bootstrap confidence intervals show that the scale effect is not attributable to spatial leakage, to the annotation rule, or to the baseline architecture. Comparison with an independent 10 m land-cover product shows that the gain from context is concentrated where CLC labels generalise over heterogeneous ground.
evidence_items.title: SENSERO: A Multi-Scale, Multi-Label Sentinel-2 Benchmark for Romania with Cross-Scale Land-Cover Classification Baselines

evidence_items.summary: Data Desa Presisi integrates narrative village monographs and structured census records, creating challenges for contextual, numerical, and cross-source information access. This study designed and evaluated a locally deployed, route-aware, evidence-grounded retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chatbot that combines deterministic DuckDB queries, document retrieval, provenance, and privacy-aware routing. Evaluation used 100 ground-truth questions from Setu and Gunung Putri. Eighty-four database, monograph, and mixed-evidence questions were assessed using RAGAS and ROUGE-L, whereas 16 conversational and policy questions were evaluated through deterministic checks. Elasticsearch at a temperature of 0.1 produced the highest composite score (0.592018), although post hoc Wilcoxon tests found no statistically significant superiority over alternative configurations. The selected configuration achieved a 98.0% functional pass rate and a 97.92% numeric-match rate. Public-mode usability evaluation involving 21 village officials and staff yielded 96.03% effectiveness. Scalability testing covered pipeline construction and retrieval across 30 census inputs and 28 monographs, but did not assess concurrent users or full end-to-end production workloads. These findings provide preliminary evidence that route-aware RAG can improve transparent, evidence-grounded access to heterogeneous village data while preserving deterministic handling of numerical queries and privacy-sensitive information.
evidence_items.title: Design and Evaluation of a Route-Aware, Evidence-Grounded RAG Chatbot for Accessing Village Monographs and Census Data within Data Desa Presisi

evidence_items.summary: Rapid urbanization and consumption growth have intensified the need for locally relevant solutions that translate environmental awareness into measurable individual action which is a priority of the Saudi Vision 2030 and the Saudi Green Initiative. While gamified eco-feedback applications show promise, most rely on passive monitoring, lack cultural localization, and offer no mechanisms to verify that pro-environmental actions actually occur. This paper presents Nameer, an Arabic-first mobile application integrating gamification, agentic AI, and automated real-world task verification within a behavioral-intervention framework grounded in the Fogg Behavior Model and Design Science Research methodology. Personalized sustainability tasks are generated by autonomous agents using a Wilson-score preference model, while authenticity is confirmed through image classification, a hybrid vision–OCR pipeline, GPS-based checks, and AI-generated quizzes; a carbon-footprint module quantifies each completed action’s impact. System-level evaluation and a formative usability study combining scenario-based testing with the System Usability Scale showed that the image-classification model reached 87.0% accuracy, the recommendation engine achieved an F1-score of 0.87, and the platform recorded a measurable carbon offset during the pilot. These findings, drawn from an initial proof-of-concept prototype, suggest that combining behavioral design, agentic AI, and verified action offers a promising technical foundation for community-driven urban sustainability aligned with UN SDGs 11 and 12; longitudinal behavioral impact remains a subject for future investigation.
evidence_items.title: Leveraging Gamified Digital Interventions for Urban Sustainability in Saudi Arabia: Design and Development of an Arabic-First Agentic AI Mobile Application

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Purpose Canine leishmaniasis is one of the most important endemic zoonotic diseases in Latin America, affecting thousands of individuals. Treatment in dogs commonly involves the use of agents with leishmanicidal activity such as allopurinol, typically administered in combination with miltefosine or meglumine antimoniate. Long-term management frequently relies on the off-label use of human formulations (100 or 300 mg tablets), requiring tablet splitting to achieve dose adjustment for infected dogs, which may compromise dosing accuracy. Methods To address this limitation, allopurinol printlets were developed using semi-solid extrusion (SSE) 3D printing (ALLO-3D) to enable dose personalization for small- to medium-sized dogs. The drug dissolution and release kinetics of the printlets were investigated. The greenness profile of the 3D printing was evaluated using the Index of Greenness Assessment of Printed Pharmaceuticals (iGAPP). Results The optimized formulation, composed of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), lactose monohydrate, croscarmellose sodium (CCS-Na), and a water–ethanol (7:3, v/v) binder solution, exhibited an immediate-release profile (Q = 75%; 45 min). The developed printlets showed a mean weight of 390.1 mg (RSD = 1.65), drug content of 39.83 ± 0.75 mg printlet⁻¹, and content uniformity of 104.74 ± 2.36% (AV = 5.4). All quality control tests complied with the requirements established in the official codes for oral solid dosage forms. The drug release profile was best described by the First-order model (R² > 0.95). Conclusion These findings demonstrate that SSE 3D printing represents a promising strategy to produce personalized printlets containing allopurinol, enabling accurate dose adjustment and potentially improving therapeutic management in canine leishmaniasis. Additionally, the ALLO-3D manufacturing process proved to be suitable from an environmental impact perspective according to the iGAPP metric.
evidence_items.title: Development and Evaluation of 3D Printed Allopurinol Tablets for Veterinary Use

evidence_items.summary: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.
evidence_items.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Agent-evolution methods use execution feedback to improve prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration, but their implementations often rebuild the same experimental machinery. We present RSIHub, an open-source framework for building, comparing, and extending these methods on shared infrastructure. Recipes compose reusable operators and declare mutable resources; RSIHub supplies execution, evaluation, recovery, and lineage. Researchers can focus on evolution policy while evaluation stays outside the mutable surface and results remain tied to candidates and evaluation conditions. We instantiate AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, and GEPA without modifying the framework core, keeping method-specific logic in recipes and operators. We evaluate them with MiniSWE and Codex on Terminal Bench 2 and τ^3 Banking under fixed model and evaluator configurations. The largest observed overall pass@1 gain is 13.5 percentage points, while method rankings vary across settings and optimization gains do not always transfer to held-out tasks. RSIHub provides a common protocol for comparing evolution policies, inspectable candidate histories, and reusable components for developing new methods.
evidence_items.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods

evidence_items.summary: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano. Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks. Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.
evidence_items.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain

evidence_items.summary: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution. A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control. This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run. This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.
evidence_items.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training

evidence_items.summary: Building virtual embodied agents that operate in open-ended games like human players is a long-standing goal requiring both long-horizon autonomy and reliable native-interface control. As a procedurally generated open world, Minecraft provides a natural testbed for studying the integration of these capabilities. Existing agents typically provide either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning executed through environment APIs or predefined skills. To bridge this gap, we propose HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness. At the orchestration level, we equip the harness with structured memory for tracking progress and a VLM planner for selecting subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. To reliably determine subtask completion, we further introduce a policy-coupled task completion state detector that conditions on VLA policy context to signal candidate completion. At the control level, a single VLA executes all subtasks with vision-only perception and native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between heterogeneous GUI and non-GUI interactions, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings. We also train the VLA through world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with environment feedback to improve reliability and recovery. HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, while also completing long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch like human players.
evidence_items.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games

evidence_items.summary: A live esports broadcast needs a director who chooses which camera goes on air and a caster who talks over that choice, every second and without knowing what comes next. Streaming video language models have learned to commentate, but only over a broadcast that a human director has already produced. We study live broadcast production, in which a model receives the raw camera of every player and must both direct and commentate from the past alone. We present DirCast, a single streaming video language model that does both. Every second it scans all cameras at low resolution, decides with a hold-or-switch director whether and where to cut, and reads the chosen camera at high resolution before it speaks. Its context keeps what went on air and what was said and lets the other views expire, which bounds the cost of a stream of any length. We build a dataset of 27 professional Dota 2 matches with a camera for every hero, the human director's choices and the casters' commentary. DirCast directs better than rule-based and zero-shot directors including GPT-5, and its commentary wins 29.2 percent of comparisons against GPT-4o under the Proact-VL protocol, against 19.4 percent for the strongest of eleven streaming commentators that watch the human broadcast.
evidence_items.title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model

evidence_items.summary: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness. During team training, the frozen Teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision for the Searchers, while the Leader learns from team success and the Answerer from candidate correctness. Across seven datasets, the trained system reaches 38.68% macro avg@4, exceeding Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL, the trained cascaded multiagent system, by 2.61 percentage points. The team also solves more questions within four attempts.
evidence_items.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation

evidence_items.summary: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and strong cross-architecture generalization of OWP. Using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B as the backbone, OWP improves performance by 12.9 and 8.6 points on CMM and AVHBench, respectively, while consistently achieving gains of 0.67-2.25 points across four general OLLM reasoning benchmarks. Furthermore, OWP generalizes effectively to VideoLLaMA2-AV, improving performance by 4.6 and 3.9 points on the same benchmarks. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZiiJianLiu/Omni-Woodpecker
evidence_items.title: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs

evidence_items.summary: Structured knowledge retrieval acquires task-relevant evidence from structured knowledge sources for downstream tasks. Existing methods rely on unconstrained retrieval or predefined query-rule supervision, such as author-paper rules for scientific discovery and anatomy-drug rules for precision medicine. Such supervision is rarely available in practice. We propose Co-Adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining Retrieval (CoRE), which jointly learns which reasoning rule to assign to each query and how to retrieve evidence under that rule, without predefined query-rule pairs. A routing agent selects a rule, and its corresponding retriever traverses the knowledge base and ranks evidence that satisfies the rule's constraints. Because routing and retrieval are interdependent, CoRE alternates between reinforcement learning for the routing policy and contrastive learning for the rule-constrained retriever. The selected rules provide supervision for retriever training, while retrieval performance rewards the routing policy. This closed-loop process enables both components to co-adapt without explicit query-rule supervision. Experiments on STaRK-QA datasets across scientific discovery, biomedical reasoning, and e-commerce knowledge management demonstrate CoRE's effectiveness. Ablations show the benefit of co-adapting the router and retriever. Generation-based routing transfers across datasets and benefits from multi-domain pretraining followed by target-specific fine-tuning. Analysis of rule usage across queries also informs automatic rule refinement and discovery.
evidence_items.title: Co-adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining for Structured Knowledge Retrieval

evidence_items.summary: Slider-based control aims to give users continuous, fine-grained control over the intensity of individual edits in instruction-based image editing. However, existing approaches fail to deliver reliable continuous controllability: traversing a slider can produce abrupt visual jumps and non-monotonic changes, while jointly controlled sliders can interfere with one another. To systematically study these limitations, we introduce SlideBench, a comprehensive benchmark for continuous image editing spanning diverse editing categories and equipped with a unified suite of metrics quantifying monotonic progression, perceptual continuity, and inter-slider disentanglement. Building on these observations, we propose SliderEdit++, which explicitly regularizes the intermediate editing trajectory rather than supervising only its endpoints. Our method combines velocity- and semantic-space trajectory regularization with spectral control to encourage smooth, predictable slider traversal, together with a disentanglement objective that reduces interference between independently controlled edits. On SlideBench, SliderEdit++ achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the overall score by 18.5% relative to the strongest baseline. At the same time, using a few-step editing backbone makes our method approximately 3x to 20x faster than existing slider-based approaches, enabling substantially more responsive interactive editing.
evidence_items.title: SliderEdit++: Improved Slider Trajectories in Instruction-Based Image Editing
